items.text: the very first requirement in a Hospital that it should do the sick no harm
items.speaker: Florence Nightingale
items.context: Nightingale opens the preface by saying it may seem a strange principle to state, then names it as a hospital's first requirement. The text is a verbatim extract of that sentence.

items.text: A teacher affects eternity; he can never tell where his influence stops.
items.speaker: Henry Adams
items.work: The Education of Henry Adams, ch. 20
items.context: Adams, a historian, was hired to teach medieval history at Harvard and reflected on teaching in his autobiography.

sources.title: Henry Brooks Adams - Oxford Reference
sources.publisher: Oxford University Press (Oxford Dictionary of Quotations)

items.text: The secret of the care of the patient is in caring for the patient.
items.speaker: Francis W. Peabody
items.work: The Care of the Patient, Journal of the American Medical Association
items.context: Peabody was an American physician. The line comes from his 1927 JAMA essay, listed in the sourced section of Wikiquote. In the essay it appears mid-sentence, after "for".

items.text: Trust yourself. You know more than you think you do.
items.speaker: Benjamin Spock
items.work: The Common Sense Book of Baby and Child Care (Dr. Spock's Baby and Child Care)
items.context: Wikiquote says this is the book's first sentence, printed under the heading "Trust Yourself", and often quoted with those words added.

items.text: You matter because you are you, and you matter to the last moment of your life.
items.speaker: Cicely Saunders
items.work: Quoted in Robert Twycross, 'A Tribute to Dame Cicely Saunders' (memorial service, 2006)
items.context: Saunders was an English nurse and physician. The quote is widely cited as her words and is the founding idea of the modern hospice movement.
